svg.aria-label: Comparison of the STM32MP157F-DK2 and STM32MP257F-DK boot chains: the 32-bit board has no BL31 and no DDR firmware, OP-TEE is its secure monitor and serves clocks, resets and voltage domains, and the SD card works with the stock device tree; the 64-bit board has a resident BL31, DDR training firmware, a clock-and-reset-only SCMI server and a patched device tree. Both share the GPT SD image rules, the FIP and the same pinned releases.
svg.text: STM32MP157F-DK2 and STM32MP257F-DK: one family, two boot chains
Same ROM-to-BL2-to-FIP idea and the same SD image rules; a shorter chain and a smaller memory on the 32-bit chip.
this board: 2 x Cortex-A7, 512 MiB DDR3
the 64-bit sibling: 2 x Cortex-A35, 4 GiB LPDDR4
GPT, rootless assembly, extlinux.conf on the bootable partition
fsbl1, fsbl2 (ROM looks them up by name)
type GUID 19d5df83-..., or the name fip; no FWU metadata
BL31, OP-TEE (2 files), U-Boot, 3 DTBs, DDR FW: 8 entries
OP-TEE's own scmi-msg: clock, reset, voltage
Arm SCP-firmware in OP-TEE: clock, reset only
served over SCMI: stock device tree boots
not served: patched device tree boots
Debian armhf / Alpine armv7 (needs qemu on any PC but a 32-bit ARM one)
Green = the same on both boards, amber = differs. Facts from docs/14-the-stm32mp-family.md; both boards are built from the same upstream releases.
